constraints.text: One WM-PER-001 Person anchor is permitted per declared identity domain; source records, accounts, identifiers, documents and credentials remain separate record-plane objects.
HRIS, ATS, directory, LMS and future source systems are local bindings and projections, never universal Person masters.
Profile steward, Person anchor authority, attribute source, source-system custodian and disclosure controller are distinct roles.
Registrar-copied facts carry source and assurance and are corrected only through the source authority; local correction creates a dispute/proposal, not a replacement fact.
Every in-profile attribute and disclosure carries assurance flag and attribute-source reference.
AccountBinding is not a profile member; it is an auditor-introduced, identifier-unassigned deferred candidate outside this contour.
Account deprovisioning never deletes or changes the Person anchor.
Reference identifiers require origin class; where no qualified identifier exists, the profile maintains an unlinked local binding or proposed link rather than fabricating an anchor match.

Deterministic linkage is prohibited unless every carrier exists for scheme, scheme version, issuer, authority/domain scope, value, referent kind, non-reassignment policy, active status and overlapping validity.
Qualified identifiers are opaque; pointer equality, normalization, inferred issuer/tenant/namespace or truncated/transliterated/native name equality never establishes identity.
Biometrics, pseudonyms, contact points, display names, name plus date of birth and similarity scores never serve as deterministic keys.
Non-deterministic linkage remains proposed and carries direction, asserting system, state, rule version, purpose, validity, authorising role, evidence and confidence or explicit absence.
Probable matching cannot activate asserted state; intra-system dedup follows the same contract.
Merge, split and reversal are addressable decisions; distinct anchors, non-reassignable superseded identifiers, resolvable tombstones and reversal paths are preserved.
Identity proofing may be absent or not-proofed; not-proofed status cannot authorize elevation or deterministic merge.
Names are structured, script-aware, effective-dated assertions; corrections supersede, changes close/open intervals, and fabricated former names are forbidden.
Former names are default-suppressed; lawful release requires named purpose, basis, relying-party class and audit record.
Pseudonyms and local identifiers carry correlatability class; pairwise or single-use pseudonyms also carry derivation and scope; rotation is not claimed without an allocated carrier.
Shared, functional and delegated channels are employer/system-controlled and never person-controlled contact points or linkage evidence.
Every contact point has at least one purpose limitation; verification is time-bounded and invalidated by reassignment or failed control.
Contact verification proves channel control only and never Person identity.
Disclosure prefers a predicate over an attribute whenever sufficient and logs purpose, basis, relying-party class and released set to a person-readable audit service.
Link and proposal records are sensitive and excluded from default projections.

Administrative sex and gender-recognition dates are out-of-profile governed references; self-identified gender is person-controlled special-category data only; former-name suppression remains explicit.
Residence is default-suppressed and, if retained, has a restricted residence kind; biometric pointers are special-category and default-suppressed.
Named projections and relying-party classes are closed and versioned; unknown classes receive no projection.
Enterprise time semantics distinguish occurrence/effective time, registration/source time and knowledge/ingestion time; absent registration time is never fabricated.
Lifecycle states are provisional and non-canonical pending inherited taxonomy holds; archiving preserves identifiers, tombstones, history and disclosure logs.
Retention and erasure classes are explicit; required tombstones and disclosure logs survive subject erasure in minimized form.
Employment, customer, role and account facts remain relationship-owned and are not Person attributes.
Civil-registration-required findings are excluded at finding level, not optionalized or populated with fabricated values.
The frozen dossier governs ContactPoint as a WM-PER-001 finding; out-of-dossier sibling identifiers and version strings are unverified and excluded.
The base is pinned by digest; registry/spec entry-kind, currency and legacy-path drift block publication.
All required compositions are dispositioned explicitly; unnamed dependencies are removed or treated as unpinned publication blockers.
de-conformance-claim-flag remains false; standards claims are alignment-only.
All v1 predecessor fields are non-normative and non-key.
Candidate and fixture digests are independently recomputed outside the frozen audit; the audit itself verified none.
All inherited holds remain verbatim, undischarged and annotated for contour relevance.
Publication and installability are refused while any hold, change request, dependency pin or fixture execution remains open.

inheritedHolds.text: Reconcile and re-pin the Core Person Vocabulary version before publication: base cites CPV 2.00 (2022-04-01), grok cites CPV 2.1.2 (2026-05-12). Properties grok relies on (Contact Point on Person, residency as Jurisdiction, the gender/sex split, GenericDate) must be confirmed against the live release actually pinned.

Reconcile the ISO/IEC 24760-1 edition: base cites the 2025 edition, grok cites 2019. Both retrievals were catalogue-level only, so no definition, identifier taxonomy or identity-record state vocabulary may be published as canonical from this standard.
Re-verify GDPR Article 9 special-category wording against the EUR-Lex OJ text; the base verified it from an unofficial reproduction (tier 3) after repeated EUR-Lex retrieval failure.
Re-verify CRPD Article 12 and General Comment No. 1 wording against an official UN-hosted text; one provider recorded an HTTP 403 at OHCHR and quoted secondary sources.

Verify every accepted source URL as live and version-pinned, including the two OASIS CIQ v3.0 URL variants, both ICAO Doc 9303 landing pages, and the UN Principles and Recommendations Rev.3 PDF whose body could not be text-extracted (paragraph-level citations are currently absent).

Run domain-profile validation on at least one non-EU profile before publication: the model is EU/UN-weighted (GDPR, eIDAS/EUDI PID, CPV, NIST levels), and a common-law vital-records plus ID-card regime and a Nordic population-register architecture must be mapped into the frame rather than assumed equivalent.

Correct the base coverage-claim counts: it states 7 bundles, 15 layers and 28 findings, but the base structure contains 14 layers; after the accepted addition the merged model is 7 bundles, 14 layers, 29 findings and 14 functions.

Scope the imported alternative-registration-routes finding on publication: only the UN LIA and CRVS-IdM backed portion (host-State or internationally mandated issuance, conferral by an identification authority linked to civil registration, delayed registration) may be presented as sourced; foundling, unknown-parentage and presumed-death-restoration sub-cases must be marked as unsourced operating cases, and the overlap with q-stateless-substitute must be resolved.
